parsed.note_claim: Europeans have been building bathhouses/steam baths for thousands of years, long before the Moors colonised a small corner of Europe.
parsed.label: SUPPORTS
parsed.quote: Iron Age saunas, unique to the Castro Culture of northwestern Iberia, have puzzled archaeologists since the nineteenth century. Initially interpreted as kilns, crematoriums, or ovens, their function has since been established as bathing structures
parsed.reason: The page describes Iron Age (pre-Roman) sauna/bath structures in northwestern Iberia dated to the fourth–third centuries BC, directly supporting the claim that Europeans built steam baths/bathhouses well before the Moorish period.
